newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK ethnic minorities welcome passports decision.
newsitem.headline: HK ethnic minorities welcome passports decision.

text.p: Hong Kong's ethnic minorities on Wednesday welcomed a decision by Britain to grant passports to some 8,000 mainly Indian and Pakistani residents in the territory.
The ethnic minorities had previously faced the threat of becoming stateless when China resumes sovereignty over the British colony at midnight on June 30.

"I'm absolutely delighted as you can no doubt imagine. It is the news that we have been waiting for many, many years," Ravi Gidumal, director of Indian Resources Group, told Hong Kong government radio.
The Council of Hongkong Indian Associations also welcomed Britain's decision.
"Through all this, we have kept our faith in the traditional British sense of fairness and I am glad to see that our faith was not misplaced," chairman Kewalram Sital said in a statement.
"The British sense of justice has prevailed against all odds and the ethnic minorities of Hong Kong are about to receive what is their due," Sital said.

Britain's Home Secretary (interior minister) Michael Howard said on Tuesday he had carefully reviewed the position of ethnic minorities in light of concern their nationality would be uncertain after China takes over the territory.
"It is clear that the assurances which they have been given over a number of years have not allayed this concern," Howard told parliament.
Howard said he expected the great majority of those concerned to continue to live in Hong Kong.

While they will have residency rights in Hong Kong after the handover, it was unclear whether they would be entitled to Chinese nationality and the future Hong Kong Special Administrative Region passports.
Many families of the ethnic minorities have lived in the colony for generations but only hold British travel documents and have not been entitled to settle or work in Britain.

Ethnic minority representatives have always said their community members did not want to move to Britain en masse and had every intention of remaining in Hong Kong. But they wanted guarantees they would not be stuck in a stateless limbo.
China will take over the thriving territory of six million people after more than 150 years of British colonial rule.
